inventory.name: Siemens photon-counting CT, National University Hospital

inventory.limit: This is the reporting upper bound. The exact scan day, model variant and later service at this site remain unverified.

inventory.name: GE Photonova Spectra, UW–Madison
inventory.claim: By 13 November 2026, UW–Madison had scanned its first standard-of-care patients on its FDA-cleared Photonova Spectra that autumn. The FDA cleared the device family on 20 March.
inventory.limit: The standard-of-care date is an upper bound and applies to the named operator. Its November 2022 system was a research prototype. GE’s 16 November collaboration announcement does not establish equivalent use at all participating sites.

trace: At Mayo, siemens-naeotom-alpha-photon-counting-ct progressed from investigational installation in April 2021 to clinical use later in 2021 after U.S. clearance on 30 September. The formal launch was 16 November. The FDA file and Mayo confirm distinct stages.

Canonical design trace: siemens-naeotom-alpha-photon-counting-ct builds on siemens-somatom-force-dual-source-ct, which builds on siemens-somatom-definition-flash-dual-source-ct, which builds on siemens-somatom-definition-dual-source-ct. The FDA submissions describe the carried-forward dual-source geometry and named changes. The first link explicitly carries forward Force’s geometry while changing both detector arrays from energy integration to photon counting.

A separate detector branch: siemens-somatom-count-photon-counting-ct-prototype adapted siemens-somatom-definition-flash-dual-source-ct using one photon-counting and one energy-integrating detector. Mayo installed the investigational unit in 2014. The NIH team demonstrated human abdominal imaging with an investigational unit in 2015 (Pourmorteza et al., doi:10.1148/radiol.2016152601). The batch establishes the Flash-to-CounT adaptation. A hardware inheritance link from CounT to Alpha awaits direct evidence.

At the method level, siemens-somatom-definition-dual-source-ct has a same-principle connection to existing clinical-x-ray-computed-tomography. The existing record connects early clinical CT to medical-x-ray-projection-imaging. Scope is the imaging method and does not imply that the EMI detector hardware carried over.

On the silicon branch, ge-photonova-spectra-silicon-photon-counting-ct evolved from GE’s Revolution Apex hardware according to the GE technical filing K253520. UW documented evaluation of a 2022 silicon prototype and began standard-of-care scanning with the cleared product in autumn 2026. Revolution Apex has no canonical record in this batch.
alternatives: ge-photonova-spectra-silicon-photon-counting-ct uses silicon, canon-ultimion-photon-counting-ct uses cadmium zinc telluride and siemens-naeotom-alpha-photon-counting-ct uses cadmium telluride. These are documented parallel product branches. Independent invention and technical transmission between companies remain open.

An earlier dedicated branch used spiral photon-counting CT to scan referred women, reported by Berger and colleagues in 2019 (doi:10.1097/RLI.0000000000000552). Broad claims that no clinical photon-counting CT existed before 2021 exceed the whole-body scope.
Canon and National Cancer Center Japan announced clinical research with an earlier Canon system in April 2023. Canon's commercial Ultimion release concerns a later named configuration in Japan.
frontier: Find design records documenting which detector or calibration work from SOMATOM CounT and Count Plus passed into Alpha, beyond the known sequence of installations.
Locate a named Japanese operator's first routine Ultimion scans and whether an installation differs from the research units in Chiba.
Read precommercial Deep Silicon prototype publications and GE filings to trace which design elements and collaborators contributed to Photonova Spectra, including the path from Revolution Apex.
Resolve the early GE/Rabin human prototype with a contemporary operator report or full original conference proceedings before claiming any human priority.
Check the patent and hospital archive for the earlier Siemens/other manufacturers’ continuous-rotation and multislice stages; the method-level link here leaves those generations open.
screen: Searched canonical records, links, sources and leads for computed tomography, dual-source, photon-counting and scanner trade names at commit 71326e0. Retained the existing EMI clinical X-ray CT and projection radiography nodes. No matching named-generation, platform or detector lead was found. Site adoption alone was not proposed as a new record. Missing Singapore model attribution also prevented attaching the NUH deployment to Alpha.
coverage: Evidence inspected through 17 November 2026. Selected examples are bounded to the documented sites and Japanese market. Later service, regional penetration, global priority and clinical effectiveness are not estimated.
